::: {#exm-permutation-equivariance}

#### A GRU is not permutation equivariant

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
_ = torch.manual_seed(0)
gru = nn.GRU(8, 8, batch_first=True)
with torch.no_grad():
    gru_out, _ = gru(x)
    gru_reversed, _ = gru(x_reversed)
gru_gap = (gru_reversed - gru_out.flip(1)).abs().max().item()
print(gru_gap)
```

A [GRU](rnns.qmd#def-gru) layer given the same `r py$n_line` vectors forwards and backwards does not just reverse its outputs:
the largest difference between the two is `r sprintf("%.2f", py$gru_gap)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1g", py$reverse_gap)` for [self-attention](#def-self-attention) in @sol-reverse.
Each [hidden state](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-hidden-state) depends on the vectors before it,
so the GRU is not [permutation equivariant](#def-permutation-equivariance).

:::
